transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-25 16:00 PDT | Duration 62m | Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Chen (CTO - Novara), Evan Brooks (Head of IT - Novara), Priya Sharma (Compliance)

Summary (auto): High-level discovery on air-gapped on-prem deployment needs, security/compliance constraints, and PoC next steps. Red flags: need for offline update package signed by Redwood, strict change control, and aged GPU fleet on some sites.

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick around the table? We'll keep this high level then dive into the technical questions.
[00:12] Dr. Maya Chen: Hi, Maya here. CTO, overseeing ML infra and lab deployments.
[00:18] Evan Brooks: Evan, head of IT. I manage the data center and firmware policies.
[00:22] Priya Sharma: Priya, compliance. I'll focus on FDA/HIPAA + audit trails.
[00:28] Lena Ortiz: Great. Samir's our SE, he'll cover runtime/ops details. Samir, over to you.
[00:35] Samir Patel: Thanks Lena. So at a high level Redwood Private supports a VPC-hosted private control plane or fully air-gapped on-prem deployments. For air-gap we ship an appliance bundle and a signed, versioned offline update package.
[00:48] Priya Sharma: Quick question — "signed package" means HSM-backed signatures? We need non-repudiation for FDA audits.
[00:55] Samir Patel: Yes, the packages are signed using our signing key; we can integrate with customer HSMs for key rotation if needed. We also produce checksums and audit manifests.
[01:05] Evan Brooks: Can you describe the offline update flow? Our sites don't have internet, and procurement only allows USB-carry-in after QA.
[01:12] Samir Patel: Sure. Typical flow: Redwood generates a signed bundle (tar + manifest + signature). You receive it via secure transfer or USB. On your side an update agent verifies signature, runs integrity checks, and applies updates to the runtime. There is also an option for staged apply — you can test on a staging node, then flip to prod.
[01:30] Dr. Maya Chen: How do you handle model binaries — are they encrypted at rest? We cannot have model weights sitting unencrypted.
[01:36] Samir Patel: We support disk encryption and at-rest encryption of model shards. For air-gapped setups we recommend using customer-managed KMS or HSM that can perform decryption locally. Redwood's control plane does not store unencrypted weights.
[01:48] Priya Sharma: What about key management lifecycle? Rotation, backup, and attestations?
[01:52] Samir Patel: We support key wrapping with customer KMS, HSM-backed keys, and we can document rotation procedures. Attestation logs are included in the audit package.
[02:03] Lena Ortiz: Quick qualification — are you evaluating hosted/dedicated/private in parallel or is this purely on-prem?
[02:08] Dr. Maya Chen: It's mostly on-prem air-gapped. We considered hosted for dev but regulated products require air-gap for production.
[02:15] Lena Ortiz: Got it. Can you tell us the target workload? Latency goals? QPS?
[02:22] Dr. Maya Chen: Primarily inference for internal research tools and a downstream clinical QA assistant. Latency target is sub-500ms for short prompts in the QA path, but batch throughput matters for bulk annotation tasks. QPS is low initially — maybe 5–10 rps — but bursty during nightly jobs.
[02:37] Samir Patel: Ok that maps to small production clusters. One question on hardware: do you have GPUs at all sites? What models?
[02:44] Evan Brooks: We have a mixed fleet — a core DC has a few A100s, but our lab sites have older V100s and one location uses an AMD accelerator (we're evaluating).
[02:54] Samir Patel: Noted. For older V100s we can use quantized model variants and kernel fallbacks. AMD support is more limited on our side today, we'd need to scope that — we can run CPU-only fallback but that's slow.
[03:07] Dr. Maya Chen: If we use quantized 7B models, what kind of latency can we expect on V100?
[03:12] Samir Patel: Very approximate: quantized 7B on A100 ~50–90ms per token; on V100 maybe 2–3x worse depending on sequence length and kernel support. We'll run benchmark numbers for your exact config as part of the PoC.
[03:26] Priya Sharma: From a compliance perspective we also need full request logs, redaction options for PHI, and retention controls.
[03:35] Samir Patel: Redwood Private provides per-request tracing, token-level cost breakdowns, and configurable log retention. For PHI we have built-in redaction hooks and you can opt to never persist raw inputs by enabling in-memory-only processing for certain routes.
[03:52] Evan Brooks: Network ingress/egress — we need assurance there's no phone home. Does the deployed runtime require outbound connectivity for licensing checks?
[03:59] Samir Patel: For air-gapped deployments there's zero outbound by default. Licensing can be validated via offline signed tokens; we can also offer periodic attestations that are manually exchanged. Any optional telemetry is opt-in and can be disabled entirely.
[04:12] Dr. Maya Chen: Good. About scaling — if we want to burst to cloud for heavy training or annotation, do you have a hybrid routing option?
[04:20] Lena Ortiz: We support hybrid routing but for regulated products it usually requires clear data flow boundaries — e.g., only non-PII payloads can go to hosted. We can document the separation.
[04:29] Evan Brooks: One sticky point is firmware policy — our security team won't allow unsigned GPU firmware updates. How do you recommend we handle runtime/kernel updates that depend on new drivers?
[04:39] Samir Patel: We typically pre-validate driver/kernel combos in our lab and provide driver bundles as part of the offline package. For environments that can't update firmware we recommend model and kernel pinning to supported stacks; sometimes we ship a micro-optimized kernel that avoids changes.
[04:53] Dr. Maya Chen: Do you support KV cache persistence across restarts? We want fast warm starts.
[04:58] Samir Patel: Yes, KV cache persistence and checkpointing are supported. For air-gapped deployments the cache file is kept encrypted and we can give guidance for eviction policies.
[05:08] Priya Sharma: Auditability: Can we get attestation logs with SHA hashes of deployed binaries and a signed manifest for every update?
[05:16] Samir Patel: Absolutely — our update manifest includes checksums and signed attestations. We can add additional metadata per your audit requirements for FDA.
[05:25] Evan Brooks: What's the proposed PoC scope?
[05:28] Lena Ortiz: We were thinking a 3-month pilot: deploy Redwood Private to the core DC (A100s) and one lab site with V100, run a comparison of quantized 7B vs 13B models for your QA pipeline, and validate offline update flow and auditability.
[05:41] Dr. Maya Chen: That sounds right. Budget-wise, any ballpark for a small PoC license and support?
[05:47] Lena Ortiz: We'll put together a PoC proposal — usually a small reserved capacity for the pilot plus engineering support. Samir will estimate compute costs based on your hardware.
[05:56] Samir Patel: I'll include two scenarios: (1) pin to quantized 7B for cost/lower latency; (2) run 13B quantized for quality comparisons. Also will estimate token costs for bulk annotation runs.
[06:08] Evan Brooks: About backups — if we have to restore from backup, how do you ensure model integrity and consistency with your manifests?
[06:16] Samir Patel: Backups include signed manifests and checksums. Restore verifies signatures and integrity before bringing models online. We recommend a staged restore in a staging node then promote.
[06:26] Priya Sharma: For SSO, we use Okta. Do you support SAML/SCIM and RBAC mapping?
[06:32] Lena Ortiz: Yes, Redwood supports SAML, SCIM provisioning, and granular RBAC. In Private we can integrate to your IdP over the internal network.
[06:41] Dr. Maya Chen: What's the expected timeline for the pilot? We're targeting Q3 clinical validation.
[06:46] Lena Ortiz: If we start PoC in early July, a 3-month pilot would land in early October — that gives time for operational validation before Q3/Q4 clinical gating.
[06:56] Evan Brooks: We need an onsite validation window — our infra team will want in-person signoff for the air-gap procedure.
[07:02] Lena Ortiz: We can do that. Samir, can you be available for an onsite validation week?
[07:07] Samir Patel: Yes, I can allocate a week for onsite validation in mid-July.
[07:11] Dr. Maya Chen: A few nitty gritty — do you have a list of supported driver/kernel versions and a compatibility matrix?
[07:17] Samir Patel: Yes, I'll share the compatibility matrix. It's in our runbook; we'll tailor it for your firmware versions.
[07:24] Evan Brooks: Any special network ports used for internal control plane traffic? We lock down all egress by default.
[07:30] Samir Patel: For air-gapped deployments the control plane is local; ports are limited to internal RPC and health endpoints. We'll provide an exact port list.
[07:38] Priya Sharma: Will Redwood sign a BAA? We need HIPAA covered for clinical data.
[07:43] Lena Ortiz: Redwood has a standard BAA for enterprise customers; legal can share the template. We'll flag that for the account team.
[07:51] Dr. Maya Chen: One more — can we run a small benchmark locally before the PoC to validate perf expectations?
[07:56] Samir Patel: Yes, we can supply a benchmark container and a small test harness you can run against your nodes; results can be shared and we'll interpret them together.
[08:06] Evan Brooks: Great. About costs — are there per-token charges for Private? Or just a platform fee?
[08:12] Lena Ortiz: Private is typically a platform/license fee plus compute. For pilots we often do a fixed pilot fee. We'll include pricing scenarios.
[08:19] Dr. Maya Chen: Ok that's helpful. A last point — we have an internal policy that no third-party agent may run as root. Can the Redwood runtime avoid root privileges?
[08:27] Samir Patel: The runtime can be configured to run as non-root. For some low-level kernel interactions there are privileged helpers but we can work with your security team to minimize privileges.
[08:38] Lena Ortiz: Cool. Let's recap next steps. From Redwood: send SOC2/ISO docs, on-prem runbook, compatibility matrix, and a proposed PoC SOW + pricing. From Novara: hardware inventory, a list of compliance questions, and availability for onsite validation in mid-July.
[08:56] Dr. Maya Chen: We'll gather that and aim to have the inventory to you by 6/30.
[09:01] Evan Brooks: I'll coordinate infra availability for the onsite week.
[09:05] Priya Sharma: I'll consolidate compliance items and send them over.
[09:09] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the security pack and schedule the deep dive.
[09:14] Samir Patel: Thanks all.

References shared: security whitepaper (link: https://redwood.example.com/security-whitepaper), compatibility matrix (link: internal runbook), sample offline bundle spec (link), PoC SOW template (link).

End of transcript.
